questions.question: What is Go and why was it created?
questions.answer: Go (Golang) is a compiled, statically-typed language created by Google. Designed for simplicity, fast compilation, and efficient concurrency with goroutines.

questions.question: What is the difference between Go and other languages like Python and Java?
questions.answer: Go is compiled (not interpreted), has built-in concurrency (goroutines), simpler syntax than Java, and faster than Python. No inheritance, uses interfaces.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the 'defer' keyword?
questions.answer: defer delays function execution until surrounding function returns. Useful for cleanup (closing files, releasing locks). Deferred calls execute in LIFO order.

questions.question: What are goroutines?
questions.answer: Goroutines are lightweight threads managed by Go runtime. Thousands can run concurrently. Created with 'go' keyword. Cheaper than OS threads.

questions.question: What are channels in Go?
questions.answer: Channels enable safe communication between goroutines. Send data with <-, receive with <-. Can be buffered or unbuffered. Prevent race conditions.

questions.question: What is the difference between var and :=?
questions.answer: var declares variables with explicit type, := declares with type inference. := only works inside functions, var works everywhere. Both initialize to zero value if not assigned.

questions.question: What are interfaces in Go?
questions.answer: Interfaces define method sets. Types implicitly implement interfaces if they have matching methods. Enable polymorphism without explicit declaration.

questions.question: What is the zero value in Go?
questions.answer: Zero value is default value for uninitialized variables. int: 0, string: "", bool: false, pointers: nil, slices: nil, maps: nil.

questions.question: What is the difference between arrays and slices?
questions.answer: Arrays have fixed length, slices are dynamic. Arrays are values, slices are references. Slices are more flexible and commonly used.

questions.question: What are maps in Go?
questions.answer: Maps are unordered key-value collections. Similar to dictionaries/hash maps. Initialized with make(). Keys must be comparable types.

questions.question: What is the difference between pointers and values?
questions.answer: Pointers store memory addresses (*T), values store actual data (T). Pointers allow modification of original data, values are copies.

questions.question: What are methods in Go?
questions.answer: Methods are functions with receiver. Receiver can be value or pointer. Pointer receivers can modify receiver, value receivers cannot.

questions.question: What is a WaitGroup?
questions.answer: WaitGroup synchronizes goroutines. Add() increments counter, Done() decrements, Wait() blocks until counter is zero. Used to wait for goroutines to complete.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the 'blank identifier' (_)?
questions.answer: Blank identifier discards values. Used to ignore return values, import side effects, or satisfy interface requirements without using the value.

questions.question: How does Go handle errors?
questions.answer: Go returns errors as values (last return value). Check with 'if err != nil'. Errors implement error interface with Error() method.

questions.question: What is the select statement?
questions.answer: select waits on multiple channel operations. Executes case that's ready. Useful for multiplexing channels. Has default case for non-blocking behavior.

questions.question: What is the difference between make() and new()?
questions.answer: new() allocates memory and returns pointer, make() allocates and initializes slices/maps/channels. new() for types, make() for collections.

questions.question: What is the difference between len() and cap()?
questions.answer: len() returns current length, cap() returns capacity. For slices, can grow up to capacity. For arrays, len equals cap.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the 'range' keyword?
questions.answer: range iterates over arrays, slices, strings, maps, channels. Returns index/key and value. Can use blank identifier to ignore values.

questions.question: What is embedding in Go?
questions.answer: Embedding allows composing types by including other types. Provides method promotion. Similar to inheritance but more flexible.

questions.question: What is the difference between break and continue?
questions.answer: break exits loop, continue skips to next iteration. Both work in for loops and select statements.

questions.question: What is a mutex?
questions.answer: Mutex (mutual exclusion) protects shared data. Lock() acquires lock, Unlock() releases. Prevents race conditions in concurrent access.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the 'iota' keyword?
questions.answer: iota generates constant values. Starts at 0, increments for each constant. Useful for enums.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the 'init' function?
questions.answer: init() runs automatically when package is initialized. Can have multiple init functions. Useful for setup and initialization.

questions.question: What is the difference between exported and unexported identifiers?
questions.answer: Exported (capitalized) are accessible outside package, unexported (lowercase) are private. Controls visibility and encapsulation.

questions.question: What is the difference between string and []byte?
questions.answer: Strings are immutable sequences of bytes, []byte is mutable. Strings are for text, []byte for binary data. Can convert between them.

questions.question: What is a buffered channel?
questions.answer: Buffered channel has capacity. Send doesn't block until buffer full. Receive doesn't block until buffer empty. Useful for decoupling goroutines.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the 'goto' statement?
questions.answer: goto jumps to labeled statement. Rarely used in modern Go. Can make code hard to follow.

questions.question: What is the difference between interface{} and specific interfaces?
questions.answer: interface{} is empty interface (no methods), accepts any type. Specific interfaces require implementing methods. interface{} is less type-safe.

questions.question: What is a context?
questions.answer: Context carries deadlines, cancellation, and values across goroutines. Enables graceful shutdown and timeout handling.

questions.question: What is the difference between := and =?
questions.answer: := declares and assigns variable, = only assigns. := can only be used inside functions, = works everywhere.

questions.question: What is a package in Go?
questions.answer: Package is a directory of Go source files. Provides namespace and encapsulation. Every file belongs to a package.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the 'const' keyword?
questions.answer: const declares constants that cannot be changed. Must be assigned at declaration. Useful for fixed values.

questions.question: What is the difference between append() and copy()?
questions.answer: append() adds elements to slice and returns new slice, copy() copies elements between slices. append() can grow slice, copy() doesn't.

questions.question: What is a race condition and how to detect it?
questions.answer: Race condition occurs when goroutines access shared data without synchronization. Detect with 'go run -race' flag. Prevent with mutexes or channels.

questions.question: What is the difference between rune and byte?
questions.answer: byte is unsigned 8-bit integer, rune is Unicode code point (int32). byte for ASCII, rune for Unicode characters.

questions.question: What is type assertion?
questions.answer: Type assertion extracts concrete value from interface. Syntax: v, ok := i.(T). ok is true if assertion succeeds, false otherwise.

questions.question: What is a goroutine leak?
questions.answer: Goroutine leak occurs when goroutines are created but never terminate. Causes memory leak. Prevent by ensuring goroutines receive signals to exit.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the 'fallthrough' keyword?
questions.answer: fallthrough continues to next case in switch statement. Executes next case code without checking condition.

questions.question: What is the difference between nil and empty?
questions.answer: nil means no value assigned (uninitialized), empty means zero-length collection. nil is not equal to empty.

questions.question: What is a channel close and how to detect it?
questions.answer: close() closes channel, no more sends allowed. Receive returns zero value and ok=false. Detect with 'v, ok := <-ch'.

questions.question: What is the difference between for and range?
questions.answer: for is traditional loop with condition, range iterates over collections. range is simpler for iteration, for is more flexible.

questions.question: What is type embedding?
questions.answer: Type embedding includes another type in struct. Promotes methods and fields. Provides composition and method inheritance.

questions.question: What is a done channel pattern?
questions.answer: done channel signals goroutines to stop. Goroutines check done channel and exit. Enables graceful shutdown of concurrent operations.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the 'panic' and 'recover' functions?
questions.answer: panic() stops execution and unwinds stack, recover() catches panic. Used for exceptional situations, not normal error handling.

questions.question: What is the difference between slice and array in terms of memory?
questions.answer: Arrays allocate fixed memory, slices are views into arrays. Slices have pointer, length, capacity. Slices are more memory-efficient.

questions.question: What is the worker pool pattern?
questions.answer: Worker pool pattern uses fixed number of goroutines to process jobs. Prevents goroutine explosion. Useful for rate limiting.

questions.question: What is the difference between == and reflect.DeepEqual()?
questions.answer: == compares values directly, reflect.DeepEqual() compares recursively. reflect.DeepEqual() handles nested structures and slices.

questions.question: What is the Stringer interface?
questions.answer: Stringer interface requires String() method. Enables custom string representation. Similar to toString() in other languages.

questions.question: What is the fan-out/fan-in pattern?
questions.answer: Fan-out distributes work to multiple goroutines, fan-in combines results. Enables parallel processing and result aggregation.

questions.question: What is the difference between string and rune slice?
questions.answer: String is immutable, rune slice is mutable. String is UTF-8 encoded, rune slice is Unicode code points. Convert with []rune(string).

questions.question: What is the purpose of go.mod and go.sum?
questions.answer: go.mod declares module and dependencies, go.sum contains checksums. Enables reproducible builds and dependency management.

questions.question: What is the difference between sync.Mutex and sync.RWMutex?
questions.answer: Mutex locks for both read and write, RWMutex allows multiple readers. RWMutex is better for read-heavy workloads.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the 'type' keyword?
questions.answer: 'type' defines new types. Can create aliases or new types with different methods. Enables type safety and custom behavior.

questions.question: What is the difference between make and new for slices?
questions.answer: make() allocates and initializes slice with length/capacity, new() returns pointer to zero-value slice. make() is preferred for slices.

questions.question: What is the pipeline pattern?
questions.answer: Pipeline pattern chains goroutines where output of one is input to next. Enables composable concurrent operations.

questions.question: What is the difference between len() and cap() for strings?
questions.answer: len() returns byte count, cap() is not applicable to strings. For strings, use len() for length.

questions.question: What is the Reader interface?
questions.answer: Reader interface requires Read() method. Enables reading from various sources. Part of io package.

questions.question: What is the difference between buffered and unbuffered channels?
questions.answer: Unbuffered channels block until both sender and receiver ready, buffered channels have capacity. Buffered decouples goroutines.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the 'switch' statement?
questions.answer: switch executes one case from multiple options. More readable than if-else chains. Can use expressions or types.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the 'import' statement?
questions.answer: import includes packages for use. Can import multiple packages. Can use aliases for package names.

questions.question: What is the difference between time.Sleep() and context.WithTimeout()?
questions.answer: Sleep() pauses for duration, WithTimeout() sets deadline. WithTimeout() is better for cancellation and context propagation.

questions.question: What is the difference between if and switch?
questions.answer: if checks conditions, switch matches values. switch is cleaner for multiple cases, if is more flexible.

questions.question: What is the difference between map and struct?
questions.answer: Map stores key-value pairs (dynamic), struct has fixed fields (static). Map is flexible, struct is type-safe.

questions.question: What is the difference between sync.Once and sync.Mutex?
questions.answer: Once ensures code executes only once, Mutex protects critical sections. Once is for initialization, Mutex for synchronization.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the 'func' keyword?
questions.answer: 'func' declares functions. Can have multiple return values. Can be methods with receivers.

questions.question: What is the Writer interface?
questions.answer: Writer interface requires Write() method. Enables writing to various destinations. Part of io package.

questions.question: What is the timeout pattern?
questions.answer: Timeout pattern uses select with time.After() to limit operation duration. Prevents hanging goroutines.

questions.question: What is the difference between function and method?
questions.answer: Function is standalone, method has receiver. Methods can be called on types, functions cannot.

questions.question: What is the difference between delete() and nil?
questions.answer: delete() removes key from map, nil clears entire map. delete() is for specific keys, nil for entire map.

questions.question: What is the semaphore pattern?
questions.answer: Semaphore pattern uses buffered channel to limit concurrent access. Acquire by receiving, release by sending.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the 'return' statement?
questions.answer: 'return' exits function and returns values. Can return multiple values. Can use named returns.

questions.question: What is the Closer interface?
questions.answer: Closer interface requires Close() method. Enables resource cleanup. Part of io package.

questions.question: What is the difference between goroutine and thread?
questions.answer: Goroutines are lightweight (thousands possible), threads are heavier (hundreds typical). Goroutines are managed by Go runtime, threads by OS.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the 'in' keyword in range?
questions.answer: 'in' is not a keyword, range uses 'range' keyword. range iterates over collections with index/key and value.

questions.question: What is the difference between slice and list?
questions.answer: Slice is built-in dynamic array, list is from container/list package. Slice is more efficient, list is doubly-linked.

questions.question: What is the broadcast pattern?
questions.answer: Broadcast pattern sends signal to multiple goroutines. Close channel to broadcast (all receive on closed channel).

questions.question: What is the difference between int and int64?
questions.answer: int size depends on platform (32 or 64 bits), int64 is always 64 bits. Use int for general purpose, int64 for specific size.

questions.question: What is the Error interface?
questions.answer: Error interface requires Error() method returning string. Enables custom error types. Standard way to handle errors.

questions.question: What is the merge pattern?
questions.answer: Merge pattern combines multiple channels into one. Useful for aggregating results from multiple sources.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the 'else' statement?
questions.answer: 'else' executes when if condition is false. Can chain with 'else if'. Provides alternative execution path.

questions.question: What is the difference between string concatenation and strings.Builder?
questions.answer: String concatenation creates new string each time (inefficient), strings.Builder accumulates (efficient). Use Builder for multiple concatenations.

questions.question: What is the tee pattern?
questions.answer: Tee pattern duplicates channel output to multiple channels. Useful for broadcasting to multiple consumers.

questions.question: What is the difference between float32 and float64?
questions.answer: float32 is 32-bit (less precision), float64 is 64-bit (more precision). float64 is default for floating-point literals.

questions.question: What is the Comparable interface?
questions.answer: Comparable interface requires Equal() method. Enables custom equality comparison. Not built-in, must be defined.

questions.question: What is the or-done pattern?
questions.answer: Or-done pattern combines channel with done signal. Prevents goroutine leaks by ensuring exit on done signal.

questions.question: What is the difference between bool and int?
questions.answer: bool is true/false, int is numeric. bool cannot be converted to int directly. Different types with different operations.

questions.question: What is the difference between sort.Slice and sort.Sort?
questions.answer: sort.Slice is simpler (uses function), sort.Sort requires Sorter interface. sort.Slice is more convenient for simple cases.

questions.question: What is the bridge pattern?
questions.answer: Bridge pattern converts channel of channels into single channel. Useful for flattening nested channels.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the 'complex' type?
questions.answer: 'complex' represents complex numbers (real + imaginary). complex64 and complex128 are available. Used in mathematical computations.

questions.question: What is the Marshaler interface?
questions.answer: Marshaler interface requires MarshalJSON() method. Enables custom JSON encoding. Part of encoding/json package.

questions.question: What is the difference between time.Ticker and time.Timer?
questions.answer: Ticker repeats at intervals, Timer fires once. Ticker for periodic tasks, Timer for one-time delays.

questions.question: What is the difference between uint and int?
questions.answer: uint is unsigned (non-negative), int is signed. uint can hold larger positive values, int can hold negative values.

questions.question: What is the difference between json.Marshal and json.Unmarshal?
questions.answer: Marshal converts Go value to JSON, Unmarshal converts JSON to Go value. Marshal encodes, Unmarshal decodes.

questions.question: What is the difference between time.After and time.NewTimer?
questions.answer: After returns channel after duration, NewTimer returns Timer object. After is simpler, NewTimer allows stopping.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the 'uintptr' type?
questions.answer: 'uintptr' is unsigned integer for pointer addresses. Used in unsafe operations and cgo. Not for general use.

questions.question: What is the Unmarshaler interface?
questions.answer: Unmarshaler interface requires UnmarshalJSON() method. Enables custom JSON decoding. Part of encoding/json package.

questions.question: What is the difference between sync.Cond and channels?
questions.answer: Cond is condition variable for signaling, channels are for communication. Cond is lower-level, channels are higher-level.

questions.question: What is the difference between string and []rune?
questions.answer: String is immutable bytes, []rune is mutable Unicode code points. String is for text, []rune for character manipulation.

questions.question: What is the difference between fmt.Print and fmt.Println?
questions.answer: Print outputs without newline, Println adds newline. Both format and output values.
